subject: Integration bridging plan: canary rollout, training, and evaluation cadence (Meridian Labs)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@meridianlabs.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@meridianlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration bridging plan: canary rollout, training, and evaluation cadence (Meridian Labs)

Hi Daniel / Sarah —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Per our post-signature alignment, attached is the initial mutual action plan (MAP) that embeds the implementation cadence we discussed: a small-holder canary, a staged migration window, and a compact training track for your ops and SRE team. Key asks below so we can lock dates: 

- Confirm the preferred canary window (we proposed 2 business days, low-volume).
- Confirm the migration blackout windows we should avoid (any critical batch jobs, market close, etc.).
- Provide the list of staging IAM roles we should request (or grant us a temporary admin service account).
- Finalize training roster by EOD Wednesday (names + roles).

High-level milestones in the attached MAP: 
1) Staging access & smoke tests (Week 0)
2) Canary (Week 1, 48h observation)
3) Incremental migration (Week 2–3, phased by tenant)
4) Training & handback (parallel during Week 2)

Acceptance criteria for canary are called out in the MAP (error rate < 0.5%, latency p95 within SLO, no data loss on KV cache handoffs). We also included a short evaluation plan template for the first two weeks of the canary (simple prompt set + traffic synthetic).

Attachments: Meridian_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (Excel, 14 KB), canary-schedule-v1.csv (CSV, 3 KB)

Can you confirm the items above and flag any must-not-change dates on your side? If you prefer, we can run the canary over a weekend to minimize customer impact.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM serving

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@meridianlabs.com>

Subject: Re: Integration bridging plan: canary rollout, training, and evaluation cadence (Meridian Labs)

Kimberly / team —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick notes from Meridian: 

- We can do a weekend canary, Saturday->Sunday looks clean for us (no regulatory batch).
- Migration blackout: please avoid pushing changes on the first business day of month close (25th–27th window in May) — we'll flag in calendar.
- Staging access: we prefer to add Redwood service account(s) to our dev-staging project with the following IAM roles: staging-deployer, secret-reader, logs-writer. I'll send a separate email with the exact role names to procurement.
- Procurement requests SOC 2 Type II evidence and our standard security questionnaire; can you point me to the SOC 2 report and a single contact at Redwood Security? Procurement is cc'd here (procurement@meridianlabs.com).

Also, can you share the evaluation prompt set you mentioned? We'd like to review it before the canary.

Thanks —
Daniel Cho
VP Product Operations, Meridian Labs
daniel.cho@meridianlabs.com | +1 617-555-0103

Attachments referenced: procurement-intake-form.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@meridianlabs.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 10:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration bridging plan: canary rollout, training, and evaluation cadence (Meridian Labs)

Thanks Daniel — great questions. Quick responses and clarifications inline below.

- Canary timing: Saturday->Sunday works. We'll run a synthetic load that mirrors 10% of your peak; evaluation window is 48 hours with a 24-hour post-canary stabilization observation.

- Migration blackout: noted on May 25–27. We'll avoid major cutovers during that window; small config flips (non-disruptive) are allowed with prior notice.

- SOC 2 & security contact: attaching a link to the latest SOC 2 summary and our security liaison: security@redwood.com (lead: Irene Cho).

- Evaluation prompt set: attached as a short CSV (see canary-schedule-v2.csv) and available here: https://drive.google.com/meridian/ev-sets. Acceptance criteria (copied from MAP):
   * Error rate (5xx or failure to respond) < 0.5% over the canary window
   * Latency p95 < 300ms (staging baseline + 20%)
   * Memory/CPU for target pods remain < 80% under synthetic load

- Fallback & rollback: if we hit failure thresholds, automated rollback to the previous model variant + config snapshot will be executed; we will keep the KV cache warm for the rollback window to avoid cold-start regressions. Recovery timeline target is < 30 minutes for most regressions.

- Training: proposed two half-day sessions (Theory + Hands-on) for ops and SREs on Tuesday & Wednesday (Week 2). Trainer: Karthik Iyer (in CC). We'll circulate the training-roster.pdf with attendee names once you confirm.

Attachments: canary-schedule-v2.csv (CSV, 4 KB).

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0147

Subject: Re: Integration bridging plan: canary rollout, training, and evaluation cadence (Meridian Labs)

Daniel / team —

Following up on staging IAM and training logistics. Two operational notes: 

1) Staging access: Please create a service account for "redwood-canary-runner@meridian-staging" and grant the roles Marissa listed; if you prefer, we can share a short Terraform snippet to apply the IAM bindings. We will need a kubeconfig with a time-limited context for the canary run.

2) Training dates: Karthik and I can run the hands-on on Tue/Wed Week 2 (09:00–13:00 PT). Please confirm timezone for your ops leads and provide attendee emails so we can create lab accounts ahead of time. We attached the training-roster.pdf draft.

On the fallback sequence, we'll include a firebreak manual-checkpoint at T+6h to validate logs and metric trends before a full migration continues. That gives your on-call team a deterministic pause to confirm stability.
